newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-MYLLYLAE WINS GOLD IN DEMANDING 50-KM.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-MYLLYLAE WINS GOLD IN DEMANDING 50-KM.

text.p: Powerful Finn Mika Myllylae tamed demanding conditions to win the final race of the Nordic skiing world championships, Sunday's 50-km classic.
Myllylae clocked a provisional winning time of two hours 16 minutes 37 seconds in heavy rain to take his first major title.

Norwegian Erling Jevne was second 54.90 seconds behind while his compatriot Bjorn Daehlie, who led for some 30 kilometres, had to be content with bronze one minute 58 seconds behind the winner, according to unofficial results.
Daehlie, looking for his fourth gold medal in the 10-day festival, made the strongest start but could not maintain his pace on sticky snow.
Myllylae went ahead for the first time after 33.3 kilometres.

The 27-year-old Finn, who had already won two silver medals and one bronze in the Trondheim championships, went away from his closest pursuers on the last of three laps of a bumpy circuit to take gold at last.
